assessment: Mika and colleagues reconstruct the evolution of uterine endometrial transcriptomes during pregnancy from 23 diverse species of mammals that differ with respect to their degree of placental invasiveness. Through this analysis, the authors infer that the eutherian mammal ancestor had an invasive mode of placentation and that the degree of invasiveness of placentation is reflected on uterine endometrial gene expression during pregnancy. Thus, phylogenetic analysis of gene expression profiles of different mammals groups them on the basis of the degree of placental invasiveness, a quite striking finding.
